Subject: Acme Health — deployment mode & SOC2/BAA follow-up

Hi Sara —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking through Acme's use case. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Primary constraint: processing PHI for clinical workflows (patient notes + scheduling). BAA required, SOC 2 Type II evidence requested, and Acme's security team needs proof of audit logs and retention windows.
- Expected traffic: intermittent bursts tied to night batch jobs + steady small-volume API calls during business hours. Latency SLO target: ~200-300ms p95 for synchronous calls.
- Key question: does Acme prefer us to host (Redwood hosted API with BAA), reserve Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pool), or pursue Private (VPC/on-prem) given the audit and control requirements?

Deployment options (high level):
1) Hosted API + BAA: fastest onboarding. We provide SOC 2 Type II attestation, BAA, and can restrict data residency to US regions. Good if Acme is comfortable with Redwood-managed infrastructure and standard audit controls.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool and stronger isolation. Predictable throughput and data separation; access controls and longer retention settings available. Common middle ground for larger customers who want isolation without on-prem.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full control for regulated environments — customer-managed networking, optional KMS/HSM, and on-prem installs for air-gapped needs. Best when legal/audit teams require customer-managed keys or physical access controls.

Attachments I’m sharing (see attached): Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf (attestation), Redwood_BAA_Draft_20270910.docx (editable draft), Redwood_PSI_PenTest_Summary_2027.pdf (high-level pen test summary).

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll drop the SOC2 attestation and BAA draft (attached). Please confirm if the redline needs are legal or security-specific.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) and Neha (security) to walk deployment modes, KMS options, and logging/audit details.
- Can you share Acme’s minimum evidence list (SOC2 report, pen test, data-flow diagrams, audit window) and any procurement timeline?

If you’re open, I can propose a mutual action plan with milestones (tech deep dive, legal review, pilot timeline) in the next email.

Thanks —

Dylan Brooks

Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers inline and an agenda for the deep-dive: 

1) Hosted audit logs & retention: Yes — our hosted API exposes per-customer audit logs (API call, actor, timestamp, request/response md5) and retention can be configured up to 24 months on enterprise plans. We can provide exports for SOC/audit purposes.

2) KMS: For Hosted we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS integrations in certain regions — that is usually a Dedicated or Private feature set when customer-managed HSMs are required. We’ll detail the options in the deep-dive.

3) Evidence & timeline: Attached are the SOC2 attestation (PDF) and pen test summary. For timelines: Dedicated provisioning typically takes 2-4 weeks after contract; Private (VPC/on-prem) is 6-10 weeks depending on on-site discovery and network approvals. I’ll include a rough cost delta in the mutual action plan.

Proposed technical deep-dive agenda (30-45min):
- Marissa: architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), expected performance profiles, and demo config.
- Neha: security controls, SOC2 scope, audit log exports, KMS/HSM options, and support for redaction in SOC artifacts.
- Q&A: procurement & legal clarifications.

I’ve attached a draft BAA (Word) — if you’re comfortable, we can send via DocuSign for an initial signature, or your legal can redline and return.
